title: Windward Health - runtime sizing and terraform refactor proposal
content:
Purpose and audience:
This note captures a proposed private deployment plan for Windward Health (pilot -> phased rollout) focused on runtime sizing, Terraform module refactor recommendations, an upgrade/migration sequence, and open questions/assumptions. Intended audience: Solutions Eng, Infra, Customer IT, and Windward Security.

Summary (one paragraph):
Windward expects an initial set of inpatient-facing and claims-processing endpoints. We propose a two-phase on‑prem pilot: a single-region production pilot sized for 150 RPS (mixed short chat and doc-summary workloads, ~200k tokens/day) with autoscaling headroom to 300 RPS. Core runtime will run Llama-family 13B as primary and 70B-vicuna style as failover for long-form; quantized 4-bit models are recommended. Terraform will be refactored into composable modules (cluster, gpu-pool, networking, kms-integration, monitoring) to support iterative upgrades without service-wide replacements.

Target SLOs and KPIs:
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens); p95 <= 1s for extended generation workloads.
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for production routes.
- Cost/Throughput target (on-prem unit economics): <= $0.0015 per generated token on average, target optimizations through batching and cache.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Customer will provide racks with nvlink-capable NVIDIA GPUs (recommended H100 80GB or A100 80GB). We assume H100 availability for pilot; fallback to A100 is supported but requires tuning.
- Storage: dedicated NFS for model artifacts and persistent KV cache; 100TB usable storage initially.
- Network: 10GbE internal with VXLAN overlay; ability to configure BGP peering to Redwood control-plane endpoints for telemetry is available.
- KMS: Windward prefers HSM-backed KMS (Entrust/YubiHSM) with a cloud-sync option; Redwood will integrate with HashiCorp Vault if requested.
- Compliance: PHI constraints require zero model telemetry leaving the customer VPC unless explicitly permitted.

Sizing recommendation (pilot region):
- Serving pool (primary 13B): 3 nodes x H100-80GB (each node hosts 2 concurrent 13B workers with shard affinity) -> target steady throughput ~120–180 RPS depending on prompt mix.
- Large model fallback pool (70B quantized): 2 nodes x H100-80GB with ZeRO-style sharding + quantization to 4-bit (caveat: quality regression testing required).
- Controller + control-plane services: 3x small CPU instances for leader election + orchestration (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM each).
- Management + monitoring: 2x instances for Prometheus long-retention, 1x Grafana instance.
- Storage: 100TB NFS for artifacts, 2x 1TB NVMe local for per-worker KV cache hot tier.

Estimated headroom and scaling path:
- A single additional H100 node in the primary pool increases throughput by ~30–40% for short prompts.
- Autoscaling policy suggestion: min 3, target 5, max 8 nodes for primary pool for predictable bursts. Use request-rate based scaling with cooldowns for 60s.

Terraform module refactor (high level):
Goal: modularize to support incremental changes and multiple clusters/regions. Split into the following modules:
- module/cluster (k8s cluster provisioning, CA certs, node pools)
- module/gpu_pool (node group with GPU-specific bootstrap, kernel/driver pinning, MIG config if applicable)
- module/networking (vlan, subnets, load balancers, egress rules, BGP peering snippets)
- module/kms (vault integration, keywrap policies, HSM connectors)
- module/monitoring (prometheus/grafana, loki, agent config)
- module/runtime_config (redwood runtime CRDs, model routes, resource classes)
Principles and changes:
- Make modules idempotent and small: separate lifecycle for cluster and runtime so runtime upgrades don't recreate cluster resources.
- Provider pinning: require explicit provider versions per module to avoid drift; store provider constraints in top-level tf.
- State management: move to per-module remote states with explicit dependencies (e.g., gpu_pool depends on cluster outputs).
- Immutable tags and resource names: ensure we can perform blue/green runtime updates by creating new node groups.
Terraform variable/api notes (text examples):
- vars: desired_gpu_type, gpu_count_per_node, node_shape, model_cache_size_gb, kms_provider, enable_nvlink (boolean)
- outputs: node_group_ids (list), lb_ip (string), kms_endpoint (string)
Potential migration pain points and mitigations:
- Driver/kernel mismatches: enforce AMI/OS + NVIDIA driver image via bootstrap. Provide prebuilt OS images and a validation job.
- State lock issues when multiple engineers run apply: restrict terraform run to CI pipeline with manual approvals for production changes.
- Secrets drift: integrate Vault and avoid plaintext secret in tfstate; use transit keywrap.

Upgrade and rollout sequence (recommended):
1) Preflight checklist (customer): rack readiness, power/Cooling, network ACLs, HSM availability, IP allocation.
2) Build baseline infra using refactored modules with minimal runtime (1 node primary pool).
3) Smoke test: verify model pull, sanity generate, KV caching, and local telemetry only.
4) Load pilot traffic (shadow mode) for 72 hours to validate latency, memory pressure, and quantization quality.
5) Expand primary pool to 3 nodes, enable autoscaling to target size.
6) Canary 70B fallback route with limited traffic; run manual evals on top 100 production prompts for quality.
7) Rollout to production routes in waves (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on error thresholds (latency spike or error rate > 1%).

Rollback plan (short):
- Runtime config rollback: point route to previous model/version or alternate pool.
- Terraform rollback: do not attempt state reversion in-place; instead create new node group with previous image and cut traffic.

Operational considerations and probes:
- Health checks: per-worker liveness + readiness; token-level tracing in local logs only (default off).
- Cost telemetry: export per-token compute cost to internal billing DB.
- Quality monitoring: run nightly evals with labeled prompts from Windward to detect regressions post-upgrade.

Security and KMS integration notes:
- Use Vault as first-class secret store. Terraform module kms should mount consistent path: secret/data/redwood/windward/keys.
- HSM integration: recommend using PKCS#11 connector shim; test with an HSM emulator before production.
- Auditing: enable audit logs for model pulls, KMS key usage, and API key lifecycle events.

Open questions for Windward and implementation owners:
- Which HSM vendor and model will be available onsite? (changes keywrap recommended flow)
- Is egress of telemetry allowed to Redwood control-plane endpoints? If not, we will run full local observability and provide an offline metrics delivery plan.
- Will Windward accept 4-bit quantization for the 70B fallback after a model-quality evaluation?
- Preferred maintenance windows for kernel/driver upgrades?

Next steps / action items:
- (Aisha) Create PR for terraform module skeleton and run it in staging (GH PR reference linked).
- (Marco) Draft driver image artifacts and validation job.
- (Priya) Coordinate HSM vendor contact and provide test credentials for Vault connector.
- (Customer IT) Confirm rack network top-of-rack switch configs and BGP peering feasibility.

Appendix: quick checklist for runbook creation (deliverables)
- Model-onboarding playbook for Windward (artifact + test prompts)
- TF module README per module with example usages and outputs
- Node bootstrap images and driver pin manifests
- Rollback runbook and on-call escalation map

Notes and references:
- See linked artifacts at top for related PR and Confluence design doc.
- This is a living draft: expected updates after the first pilot run and the initial Terraform refactor PR review.

Unresolved: detailed per-prompt throughput profiling (we will run an internal load generator pegged to Windward sample prompts to refine exact node counts).

End of document.
